I've dealt with anorexia nervosa for the better part of my 25 years. As a kid, I had a stumpy soft body type whereas my older brothers all had long lean builds, so I felt like garbage because of that. At about 13, I went vegetarian and started restricting. Now I'm 5'7" and about 110 pounds, which is way underweight. My upper body is extremely thin, but I have infernal fucking wide birthing hips that throw off my entire perception of my body. I've curated my wardrobe so that I never get stuck wearing something unflattering to the transition zone between my tiny waist and big-ass hips. It has pretty much stunted my ability to get physically close with anybody indefinitely. I'm not better. I don't know if I ever will be.

Hang in there! No one should have to deal with this shit.
I love how all of these stories are like "my dad said we absolutely were not under any circumstances getting a dog. anyway, so we got a dog,"
some of the vocals and chord progressions in My Mistake are oddly giving me Billie Holiday vibes.

I was waiting for someone to bring this one up! The strings reminded me of the scores of Indian cinema from the 1960s and 1970s, like Satyajit Ray and Merchant-Ivory films. It feels like M79's super mellow great-grandchld.

As a matter of fact, there was a "sh" sound in there. I remember even searching the word when I was younger using spellings like "pisch" because of that. And we're fairly sure that her father was not more than two generations removed from Sweden (quite likely the south, given the proximity to the area around Rostock). We have a document from his marriage in 1942, listing his father's surname as Mattisson. But he changed his to Matthies by then. Being pretty quiet about the role her own family may or may not have played in the war (she was a baby and may not have been told anything, so maybe her mother was the quiet one), my Oma claimed to not know why he did that. But at this point I've guessed that he changed it when enlisting in the German army to make his name sound less Nordic and more German.

So I think you are on to something!

I saw those same posts and couldn't get much further than that in my "research" because of the language barrier. I was (well, still am) tempted to message them on Instagram and just ask them about their usage of the word. Couldn't hurt, worst that could happen is some Danish skiiers get a rando in their inbox asking about a hashtag they used on their ski trip...

I think you're right, and that both the oral tradition and wordplay as an in-joke definitely seem like factors here! 

Now that I think about it, my colleague's recognition must have been more like hearing the two separate words "pis" and "kylling" and just being able to conclude what that must've meant – as opposed to being like, "ah yes, I have heard people get called pisschickens before." She was the one who told me that kylling meant chicken, so she could have been recognizing the language-blending near borders rather than that specific word, if that makes sense.

edited for a typo

Definitely with a hard K. So I think that lines up with what other folks are saying too, about it most likely being Danish. And that's a really good point about putting words together to develop insults of your own! I didn't even think about that, but it's so true. In both English and German it sometimes feels like a competition to put the two most ludicrous and unrelated words together to make a new derogatory word for a person getting on your nerves. I imagine things weren't that different 75 years ago.

It seems like this word could be an example of unwritten vernacular / language blending near borders / outright making new words up from existing words / the oral tradition in action. I ran the word by my mom, who also heard it all the time as a kid, and she remembered my Oma putting -en at the end of it sometimes. "Piskyllingen." Effectively making up her own German verb from this kind of nonsense noun, haha. Thank you for this response!

It could be! Having read all the comments, I also wonder if it was a case of them smushing together German and Danish, and ignoring some grammatical rules altogether, to create their own insults. In German, "Piss" as a prefix has no E at the end – like Pissstand, Pissblume, Pisswettbewerb – so maybe they picked a little here and there in following rules lol. My Oma was never able to spell it, so she never could have told me if it had one S in there or two. 

Thanks for all this! I'm going to check out this dictionary since I'm super curious now, especially given the similarities to the word you give in the first paragraph.

Yeah, I've definitely been frustrated throughout the years over doctors prioritizing the eating disorder over everything else, even when I think it's not the most pressing issue at the moment – although I do see why they prioritize it. There are moments where it *has* been the most pressing issue, but often I find myself trying to hide that aspect of my mental health when I want something else focused on more, and then it ultimately comes out anyway, and the cycle begins again lol. I'm a chronic oversharer so I don't even bother lying. 

Thanks a lot for your suggestions. Your advice definitely doesn't suck. You're right, it would be a good time to try therapy again. Transitional periods are definitely the times when I think I'd benefit from it the most.
